newsitem.title: USA: Calif. building activity surged in 1996 - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. building activity surged in 1996 - report.

text.p: Construction financing in California totaled $10.7 billion in 1996, up 20 percent from $8.9 billion the year before, according to a report released on Wednesday.
Last year's total was the highest since 1991 when construction loans totaled $11.4 billion, Acxiom Corp's DataQuick Information Systems said in the report.
"If current trends stay in place, 1997 should be even stronger than last year," Mike Ela, DataQuick's president, said in a statement.

Growth in the building sector followed other economic patterns, with the San Francisco Bay area outpacing the rest of the state with a 33.7 percent year-over-year increase, and California's Central Valley with a relatively modest 8.6 percent increase, DataQuick said.
Measured in dollar volume, Wells Fargo and Co was California's most active provider of construction financing. The lending institution made 222 loans totaling $910 million.
BankAmerica Corp's Bank of America was the second most active lender with 147 loans totaling $459 million.
Acxiom/DataQuick monitors real estate activity nationwide.
